subject.title: fix(cron): allow timeoutSeconds: 0 for no-timeout mode

question: Should the Control UI expose the existing cron `timeoutSeconds: 0` no-timeout sentinel despite the availability tradeoff of unbounded cron runs?
rationale: The gateway schema and runtime already support zero, but exposing it in the UI changes what ordinary users can configure and can remove the cron wall-clock watchdog for a job.

options.title: Approve UI no-timeout support
options.body: Refresh the PR onto current main, update tests/help, and require proof that zero is saved and runs without the cron timeout.

options.title: Keep the UI positive-only
options.body: Close the linked bug and PR as not planned while leaving no-timeout available only through lower-level protocol paths.

options.title: Defer behind clearer UX
options.body: Hold this until the UI can present an explicit no-timeout control with availability warning copy rather than a hidden numeric sentinel.

recommendation.title: Approve UI no-timeout support
recommendation.body: Refresh the PR onto current main, update tests/help, and require proof that zero is saved and runs without the cron timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the affected Control UI cron edit surface is the full cron edit parity commit that introduced this validation behavior.
